AutoOrientType.summary: AutoOrientType is the layer's auto-orientation mode (Layer > Transform > Auto-Orient in AE). Encoded as 3 mutually-exclusive bits across ldta bytes 0x25 and 0x26 — see parse_layer.go's flag-bit doc. AE collapses the bits into one of four UI choices, which we mirror here.

BlendingMode.summary: BlendingMode is the layer's compositing blend mode (ldta @0x63). Values match AE's internal numbering.

Composition.summary: Composition represents an After Effects composition.

Composition.AVLayers.summary: AVLayers returns all layers backed by an audio/video source — pre-comps, footage files, solids, placeholders. Excludes camera / light / null / text / shape / adjustment-only layers (which carry no AVItem source).

Composition.ActiveCamera.summary: ActiveCamera returns the topmost enabled (Visible == true) camera layer in the comp, or nil when no enabled camera is present. AE uses this layer's transform + camera-options for the comp's render. Multiple cameras may coexist; AE picks the topmost enabled one.

Composition.AdjustmentLayers.summary: AdjustmentLayers returns all adjustment layers (IsAdjust flag set or Type classified as adjustment).

Composition.BGColor.summary: BGColor is the composition background color (R, G, B), 0..255 per channel. Decoded from cdta @0x34/0x35/0x36 (3 × uint8). Defaults to {0,0,0} (AE's default black).

Composition.CameraLayers.summary: CameraLayers returns all camera layers in the composition.

Composition.CdtaRawBytes.summary: CdtaRawBytes returns a detached copy of the comp's cdta chunk data, or nil if the comp has no cdta. It is intended for debugging and RE tools.

Composition.Comment.summary: Item-level metadata shared with Footage / Folder. Populated by parseItem from the surrounding Item LIST (cmta child + idta byte).

Composition.CompositionLayers.summary: CompositionLayers returns layers whose source is another composition (pre-comp layers).

Composition.DisplayStartFrame.summary: DisplayStartFrame returns the comp's display-start frame (DisplayStartTime × FrameRate, rounded). Setter exists already as SetDisplayStartFrame.

Composition.DisplayStartTime.summary: DisplayStartTime is the comp's display-time origin in seconds (AE scripting's CompItem.displayStartTime / displayStartFrame). Decoded from cdta @0xA4 / @0xA8 (uint32 BE dividend / divisor pair). AE writes both 0 when displayStart is 0; non-zero pair encodes start-time in seconds.

Composition.EssentialGraphicsControllers.summary: EssentialGraphicsControllers holds the comp's Essential Graphics panel controllers (exposed properties / .mogrt controls), in panel order. Empty when the comp has no EG panel.

Composition.FileLayers.summary: FileLayers returns layers whose source is a file-backed footage item (not a solid and not a placeholder).

Composition.FootageLayers.summary: FootageLayers returns layers whose source is a footage item (file / solid / placeholder).

Composition.FrameDuration.summary: FrameDuration returns the comp's total Duration as a frame count.

Composition.GuideLayers.summary: GuideLayers returns all layers marked as guide (IsGuide flag set — invisible at render but visible in the timeline).

Composition.Guides.summary: Guides holds the composition's ruler guides (AE's drag-from-ruler alignment lines; UI-only, no render effect). Decoded from the comp's Item-level LIST:Gide. See scene_guide.go.

Composition.HasAudio.summary: HasAudio reports whether any layer in the composition has its audio switch enabled (ldta @0x27 bit 1). It does NOT verify the layer's source actually carries an audio track — only that AE would attempt audio playback for it.

Composition.Height.summary: canvas height in pixels (writable via SetSize)

Composition.ItemID.summary: ItemID returns the composition's item id (mirrors the ID field). Provided so *Composition satisfies AVItem.

Composition.ItemName.summary: ItemName returns the composition's name. Provided so *Composition satisfies AVItem.

Composition.LayerByID.summary: LayerByID returns the first layer in this composition whose ID matches id, or nil if no such layer exists. ID 0 is treated as no-match (it's the sentinel used by Layer.ParentID to mean "no parent"); real AE projects start layer IDs at 1.

Composition.LayerByName.summary: LayerByName returns the first layer in this composition whose Name matches the given string, or nil if none does. Layer names aren't guaranteed unique within a comp; use LayerByID for precise identity.

Composition.LightLayers.summary: LightLayers returns all light layers in the composition.

Composition.Markers.summary: Markers holds composition-level markers (AE's timeline-top chapter markers, distinct from per-layer markers). Stored in the AEP as a pseudo-layer (`LIST SecL` named "Markers") carrying an "ADBE Marker" property — decoded with the same machinery as layer markers.

Composition.MotionBlurAdaptiveSampleLimi.summary: MotionBlurAdaptiveSampleLimit / MotionBlurSamplesPerFrame are AE's motion-blur quality knobs (Composition Settings → Advanced). Decoded from cdta @0xC4 / @0xC8 as int32 BE. AE clamps these to positive integers in the UI (defaults: 128 and 16).

Composition.MotionGraphicsTemplateContro.summary: MotionGraphicsTemplateControllerCount returns the number of Essential Graphics controllers — mirrors AE's CompItem.motionGraphicsTemplateControllerCount.
MotionGraphicsTemplateControllerNames returns the controller display names in panel order — mirrors AE's CompItem.motionGraphicsTemplateControllerName(i).

Composition.MotionGraphicsTemplateName.summary: MotionGraphicsTemplateName is the Essential Graphics / .mogrt template name (AE default "Untitled" when the comp has no EG panel). Decoded from the comp's Item-level LIST:CIF3. See scene_essential_graphics.go.

Composition.NullLayers.summary: NullLayers returns all null-object layers (IsNull flag set).

Composition.NumLayers.summary: NumLayers returns the number of layers in the composition. Equivalent to len(c.Layers); provided as a convenience alias.

Composition.PixelAspect.summary: PixelAspect is the comp's pixel aspect ratio (1.0 = square, 2.0 = anamorphic, 0.91 = NTSC D1, etc.). Decoded from cdta @0x90 / @0x94 as an integer numerator/denominator pair.

Composition.PlaceholderLayers.summary: PlaceholderLayers returns layers whose source is a placeholder footage item (AE's "Missing Footage" placeholder, opti tag = "Plac").

Composition.PrdaRawBytes.summary: PrdaRawBytes returns the comp's prda chunk Data slice (renderer-specific options), or nil if the comp has no PRin LIST. The returned bytes are a detached debugging snapshot.

Composition.Renderer.summary: Renderer is the comp's 3D rendering engine (AE Scripting's CompItem.renderer). Stored as an internal match-name string in the `prin` chunk of the comp's `PRin` LIST sibling. Examples:

Composition.ResolutionFactor.summary: ResolutionFactor is the comp's preview-resolution downsample, X and Y. AE Scripting's CompItem.resolutionFactor: [1,1]=Full, [2,2]=Half, [3,3]=Third, [4,4]=Quarter, custom pairs allowed. Decoded from cdta @0x00 / @0x02 (two uint16 BE). Default [1,1].

Composition.SetCompMotionBlur.summary: This switch is independent of the per-layer `Layer.MotionBlur` flag — a layer renders motion blur only when both switches are on.

Composition.SetDisplayStartFrame.summary: A frame-count convenience wrapper around SetDisplayStartTime: computes seconds = frame / FrameRate and delegates the cdta write to it. Errors when FrameRate is not yet set to a positive value.

Composition.SetDisplayStartTime.summary: The divisor stored is the composition's TickRate (computed from cdta offsets 0x08/0xA8). Passing 0 clears the value back to default by writing both dividend and divisor as 0, matching AE's "unset" encoding so re-parsing yields DisplayStartTime == 0. AE 2025 sometimes writes a divisor (e.g. 23976 for 29.97 fps) that doesn't exactly satisfy the ticks-per-frame times frame-count math due to small rounding artifacts; this setter and its getter use the stored pair verbatim so a round trip of a Set call gives back exactly what was set.

Composition.SetDraft3D.summary: Disables shadows, motion blur, and depth of field in the viewport for faster preview playback.

Composition.SetDuration.summary: Writes the duration as a uint32 frame count (round(seconds x FrameRate)) and requires FrameRate to already be positive. Do not call this and SetFrameRate on the same composition: SetFrameRate does not rescale the stored duration ticks, so changing the rate afterward makes AE read back a shorter or longer duration than intended.

Composition.SetFrameBlending.summary: Layers also need their own FrameBlendEnabled flag on to actually render with blending.

Composition.SetFrameRate.summary: AE splits fps into a uint16 whole part and a uint16 fractional part (numerator over 65536); this setter uses the same encoding so partial frame rates like 29.97 round-trip exactly. `Duration` is recomputed from the existing frame count so the in-memory value stays consistent. Do not call this and SetDuration on the same composition: this setter does not rescale the stored duration ticks, so AE will read back the wrong duration at the new rate.

Composition.SetPixelAspect.summary: AE writes simple integer ratios for common presets (1/1 = 1.0, 2/1 = 2.0). For fractional ratios this setter picks num = round(par x 100) and den = 100, which is accurate enough for AE's built-in PAR presets (0.91, 1.09, 1.21, 1.33, 1.46, 1.5, 2.0).

Composition.SetResolutionFactor.summary: Mirrors AE Scripting's CompItem.resolutionFactor. [1,1] = Full, [2,2] = Half, [4,4] = Quarter; custom non-square pairs are allowed.

Composition.SetShutterPhase.summary: Unit is likely degrees (AE UI shows values like -90 / +90) but that has not been independently UI-verified — the caller passes the raw int32 value as-is.

Composition.SetWorkArea.summary: Both values are encoded as dividend/divisor pairs; this setter reuses the existing divisors when non-zero (typically 600, AE's standard work-area divisor) and falls back to 600 when the existing divisor is zero. endSeconds may be less than startSeconds — AE allows that visually, giving the work area a zero or negative span — but most workflows want endSeconds greater than startSeconds.

Composition.SetWorkAreaDurationFrame.summary: Recomputes the work-area end so that end minus start equals the given frame span, keeping start fixed, then delegates to the seconds-based work-area setter.

Composition.SetWorkAreaEndFrame.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based work-area setter, preserving the existing start.

Composition.SetWorkAreaStartFrame.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based work-area setter, preserving the existing end.

Composition.ShapeLayers.summary: ShapeLayers returns all shape layers in the composition.

Composition.ShutterAngle.summary: ShutterAngle is the motion-blur shutter angle in degrees (AE UI range 0..720, default 180). Decoded from cdta @0xAE as uint16 BE.

Composition.ShutterPhase.summary: ShutterPhase is the motion-blur shutter phase offset. Decoded from cdta @0xB4 as int32 BE. Likely degrees in the AE UI's -360..+360 range (fixture value -90 plausibly matches AE's -90° UI display) but the exact unit is not independently UI-verified — surface as raw int32 and let callers interpret.

Composition.SolidLayers.summary: SolidLayers returns layers whose source is a solid footage item.

Composition.SoloLayers.summary: SoloLayers returns all layers with the Solo flag set.

Composition.TextLayers.summary: TextLayers returns all text layers in the composition.

Composition.ThreeDLayers.summary: ThreeDLayers returns all layers with the 3D-layer flag enabled (transform interpreted in 3D space).

Composition.TickRate.summary: keyframe/marker ticks per second (per-composition, not a global 8000)

Composition.TimeScale.summary: TimeScale is the per-comp ticks-per-second base used for keyframe and marker times. Alias of TickRate, provided as a naming convenience. See [Composition.TickRate] for the full notes on cdta @0x08 / @0xA8 decoding.

Composition.Width.summary: canvas width in pixels (writable via SetSize)

Composition.WorkAreaDurationFrame.summary: WorkAreaDurationFrame returns the work-area span (end − start) in frames.

Composition.WorkAreaEndFrame.summary: WorkAreaEndFrame returns the comp's work-area end as a frame count.

Composition.WorkAreaStart.summary: WorkAreaStart / WorkAreaEnd are the render-queue partial range in seconds (AE's "Work Area" — N and B in the timeline). Decoded from cdta dividend/divisor pairs at @0x1C/0x20 (start) and @0x24/0x28 (end). When AE leaves the work area "unset", it writes 0xFFFFFFFF for the end dividend; we substitute Duration so callers always see the effective range.

Composition.WorkAreaStartFrame.summary: WorkAreaStartFrame returns the comp's work-area start as a frame count.

DefaultTextRangeAdvanced.summary: Returns the Range Advanced params at their AE defaults

DeleteLayer.summary: Removes the layer at the given 0-based index in the comp's layer

EGControllerType.summary: EGControllerType is an Essential Graphics controller's type code, as stored in its CTyp chunk. Values match AE's internal controller numbering.

EGControllerType.String.summary: String renders the controller type as AE's panel label (or "unknown").

Effect.summary: Effect represents one effect instance applied to a layer (e.g. a Gaussian Blur applied to a footage layer). The MatchName identifies the effect type ("ADBE Gaussian Blur 2", "ADBE Gradient Wipe", etc.) and Parameters holds each tweakable knob as a Property. Parameter match-names are internal numeric suffixes like "ADBE Gaussian Blur 2-0001".

EssentialGraphicsController.summary: EssentialGraphicsController is one controller in the Essential Graphics panel — an exposed property / .mogrt control.

EssentialGraphicsController.Name.summary: Name is the controller's display name (from its CpS2 localized string).

EssentialGraphicsController.Type.summary: Type is the controller kind (checkbox / slider / color / ...).

EssentialGraphicsController.UUID.summary: UUID is the controller's unique identifier (the CCtl's Utf8 child), used by AE to link the controller to its source property.

Folder.summary: Folder is a project panel folder.

Footage.summary: Footage represents a source media file, an AE solid, or a placeholder.

Footage.AssetType.summary: AssetType returns the footage kind as a string: "placeholder" / "solid" / "file". Footage items with neither flag default to "file".

Footage.Comment.summary: Comment / Label — Item-level metadata (project-panel comment + timeline color chip). Populated by parseItem from the cmta + idta chunks under the Item LIST.

Footage.EndFrame.summary: EndFrame returns the footage end frame (sspc @0xB0, uint32 BE). 0 for non-sequence footage and for fixtures without a full-size sspc.

Footage.File.summary: File returns the footage source file path. Empty string for solids and placeholders. Alias of [Footage.Path], provided as a convenience.

Footage.FootageMissing.summary: FootageMissing reports whether the footage source file was missing at the time AE saved the project (per the `footage_missing_at_save` flag in sspc @0x78). Solids and placeholders never have a file, so this is always false for them (regardless of the on-disk flag bit).

Footage.HasAudio.summary: HasAudio reports whether the footage has an audio stream — true when sspc's audio_sample_rate (8 byte f64 BE at @0xA0) is non-zero. Solids and placeholders never have audio.

Footage.IsPlaceholder.summary: IsPlaceholder is true when opti tag = "Plac" (AE's placeholder footage — name + dimensions only, no source file). Mutually exclusive with IsSolid and with having a non-empty Path.

Footage.IsSolid.summary: AE solid (generated solid-color source); solids have no disk path

Footage.IsStill.summary: AE flagged this as a still image

Footage.ItemID.summary: ItemID returns the footage's item id (mirrors the ID field). Provided so *Footage satisfies AVItem.

Footage.ItemName.summary: ItemName returns the footage's name. Provided so *Footage satisfies AVItem.

Footage.MainSource.summary: MainSource returns the typed source metadata for this footage item. Returns *FileSource for file footage, *SolidSource for solids, *PlaceholderSource for placeholders. Returns nil if the footage was built outside the parser (no source chunks available).

Footage.Name.summary: display name; SetPath syncs this to the new path's basename

Footage.Path.summary: source file path on disk; empty for solids/placeholders. Writable via SetPath

Footage.SetPath.summary: The change propagates to the underlying RIFX chunks: the alas JSON's "fullpath" field is rewritten in-place, and a legacy Cpth chunk, if any, is fully replaced. The next call to Project.WriteAEP serializes the new path. Returns an error if no writable path chunk exists for this footage (solids and placeholders never had one).

Footage.SetSolidColor.summary: RGB, each channel 0..1 — alpha is pinned to 1.0, matching AE. Every layer using this solid changes color, exactly like editing the solid's settings in AE. The same byte patch is applied by the NewSolidLayer create path.

Footage.SetSolidSize.summary: Layers using the solid are not repositioned — same behavior as resizing a solid through AE's settings dialog. Shares its ship gate with SetSolidColor.

Footage.SolidColor.summary: SolidColor is the solid's RGB color in 0..1 (only meaningful when IsSolid; parsed from the opti "Soli" chunk, alpha is always 1.0).

Footage.StartFrame.summary: StartFrame returns the footage start frame (sspc @0xAC, uint32 BE). 0 for non-sequence footage and for fixtures without a full-size sspc.

Guide.summary: Guide is one composition ruler guide.

Guide.Position.summary: Position is the guide's offset in pixels — from the top edge for a horizontal guide, from the left edge for a vertical guide.

GuideOrientation.summary: GuideOrientation is a guide's binary orientation code (as stored in ldat @0).

GuideOrientation.String.summary: String renders the orientation as "horizontal" / "vertical" (or the raw code).

InterpType.summary: InterpType identifies a keyframe's interpolation mode on one side (in-side or out-side). AE stores these as single-byte enums in the keyframe block at offsets 0x04 (in-interp) and 0x05 (out-interp).

Keyframe.summary: Keyframe represents a single keyframe on a property.

Keyframe.FrameTime.summary: FrameTime returns the keyframe's time as an integer frame count (Time × owning-comp FrameRate, rounded). Returns 0 when the keyframe was built outside the parser (FrameRate unknown).

Keyframe.InSpatialTangent.summary: length 3 when present; nil for non-spatial

Keyframe.InTemporalEase.summary: length 1 for spatial+1D, length N for non-spatial N-D

Keyframe.SetFrameTime.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via the owning composition's FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based time setter.

Keyframe.SetInInterp.summary: See SetOutInterp for the out side.

Keyframe.SetInSpatialTangent.summary: Only valid for spatial properties (Position / AnchorPoint with motion path enabled). See SetOutSpatialTangent for the out side.

Keyframe.SetInTemporalEase.summary: The slice length must match the keyframe's current ease shape: a spatial property (Position / Anchor) or 1D non-spatial property takes length 1; a non-spatial N-D property (Scale 3D / Feather 2D / 4D color) takes length N.

Keyframe.SetOutInterp.summary: See SetInInterp for the in side.

Keyframe.SetOutSpatialTangent.summary: Only valid for spatial properties (Position / AnchorPoint with motion path enabled). See SetInSpatialTangent for the in side.

Keyframe.SetOutTemporalEase.summary: Mirrors SetInTemporalEase for the out side; the slice length must match the keyframe's current ease shape.

Keyframe.SetTime.summary: Uses the owning composition's TickRate, decoded at parse time from cdta.

Keyframe.SetValue.summary: For a 1D property pass a float64. For a multi-component property pass []float64 with exact length equal to the property's component count.

Layer.summary: Layer represents a layer within a composition.

Layer.AVSource.summary: AVSource resolves this layer's source to an AVItem (Composition or Footage), or nil when SourceID is 0 or the layer was built outside the parser.

Layer.ActiveAtTime.summary: ActiveAtTime reports whether the layer is on-screen at time t — visible switch enabled AND the time falls within the layer's in/out range. Mirrors AE script's `Layer.activeAtTime(t)`.

Layer.AddFont.summary: Extends the btdk Fonts array (btdk path /0/1/0) by one entry plus its dict wrapper. The new entry is serialized in the same shape AE writes, with the second dict slot marking the font as user-resolved (matching the slot AE writes for non-default fonts). Use the returned index with SetRunFontIndex to point a style run at the new font.

Layer.AlternateSource.summary: AlternateSource returns the AVItem (*Composition or *Footage) used as this layer's media-replacement override, or nil when no override is active (AlternateSourceID == 0), the layer has no slot, the layer was built outside the parser (no owning project), or the override id doesn't resolve to any project AV item. Mirrors AE script's Property.alternateSource — except we surface the override on the layer rather than on a sub-property since AE persists one id per instance.

Layer.AlternateSourceID.summary: AlternateSourceID is the AVItem id overriding this layer's source via the Essential Properties → Media Replacement workflow (AE 18+). 0 means no override is in effect (either the layer has no Essential Property slot, or it has one but the slot is unset). The slot is only persisted when AE has promoted the layer's source via `AVLayer.addToMotionGraphicsTemplateAs()` (see the override chunk pattern in `parse_layer.go::findAlternateSourceBlsi`). Use AlternateSource() to resolve to the *Composition / *Footage item.

Layer.AnchorPoint.summary: AnchorPoint returns the layer's Anchor Point property (3D), or nil.

Layer.AudioActive.summary: AudioActive reports whether the layer would produce audio output: it has a potential audio source AND the AudioEnabled switch is on. This is the design-time check; it does not consider time.

Layer.AudioActiveAtTime.summary: AudioActiveAtTime reports whether the layer would produce audio at the given time t (seconds, in the owning composition's timeline). Combines AudioActive with ActiveAtTime.

Layer.AudioGroup.summary: AudioGroup returns the layer's "ADBE Audio Group" subgroup, or nil if absent. Present on layers with audio content.

Layer.AudioLevels.summary: AudioLevels returns the layer's Audio Levels property (2D, [left, right] channel levels in dB). Present on layers with audio content; nil otherwise.

Layer.AutoName.summary: AutoName returns the layer's display name. Falls back to the source item's name when the layer has no user-set name. Empty string for layers without a source (camera/light/null/text/shape) and no user-set name.

Layer.CameraAperture.summary: CameraAperture returns the camera's Aperture property (1D, pixels). Nil for non-camera layers.

Layer.CameraBlurLevel.summary: CameraBlurLevel returns the camera's Blur Level property (1D, %). Nil for non-camera layers.

Layer.CameraDepthOfField.summary: CameraDepthOfField returns the camera's Depth of Field toggle (1D bool-as-float, 0 = off, 1 = on). Nil for non-camera layers.

Layer.CameraFocusDistance.summary: CameraFocusDistance returns the camera's Focus Distance property (1D, pixels). Nil for non-camera layers.

Layer.CameraOptionsGroup.summary: CameraOptionsGroup returns the camera layer's "ADBE Camera Options Group", or nil for non-camera layers.

Layer.CameraZoom.summary: CameraZoom returns the camera's Zoom property (1D, pixels — AE's "Zoom" field; equivalent to focal length × 35mm conversion). Nil for non-camera layers.

Layer.CanSetCollapseTransformation.summary: CanSetCollapseTransformation reports whether AE will let the user toggle CollapseTransform on this layer:

Layer.CanSetTimeRemapEnabled.summary: CanSetTimeRemapEnabled reports whether AE will let the user enable time remapping on this layer: true when the source has a non-zero duration. Still images, text layers, and shape sources don't qualify.

Layer.ClearAlternateSource.summary: Removes the media-replacement override so AE falls back to the wrapper precomp's default source. Equivalent to calling SetAlternateSource with a nil item.

Layer.ClearTrackMatteLayer.summary: Shorthand for SetTrackMatteLayer with a zero source ID and TrackMatteNone mode. Removes the explicit matte source and the matte mode in one call.

Layer.Comment.summary: Comment is the user-set layer comment (AE's "Comments" timeline column / Layer Settings dialog). Decoded from the sibling cmta chunk; "" when no cmta is present. CRLF in the source bytes is normalized to LF for Go-friendly multi-line strings.

Layer.ContainingComp.summary: ContainingComp returns the composition this layer belongs to, or nil when the layer was built outside the parser (no owning comp wired up).

Layer.EffectsParade.summary: EffectsParade returns the layer's "ADBE Effect Parade" subgroup, or nil if absent. The parade carries each effect as a sub-PropertyGroup named by the effect's match-name. For decoded effect parameter values prefer Layer.Effects (the parade tree captures the layout but does not re-parse effect parameters).

Layer.FrameBlendPixelMotion.summary: false = Frame Mix, true = Pixel Motion

Layer.FrameInPoint.summary: FrameInPoint returns the layer in-point as an integer frame count (seconds × FrameRate, rounded). Returns 0 when the owning comp's FrameRate is unknown.

Layer.FrameOutPoint.summary: FrameOutPoint returns the layer out-point as an integer frame count.

Layer.FrameStartTime.summary: FrameStartTime returns the layer start-time as an integer frame count.

Layer.GeometryBevelDirection.summary: GeometryBevelDirection returns the Bevel Direction property (1D enum, default 1; relevant for shape/text 3D layers with bevel — present on solid layers as a stub).

Layer.GeometryOptionsGroup.summary: GeometryOptionsGroup returns the 3D layer's "ADBE Extrsn Options Group", or nil if absent (2D layers, AE 23 and older).

Layer.GeometryPlaneCurvature.summary: GeometryPlaneCurvature returns the Plane Curvature property (1D, AE 24+ Advanced 3D renderer; for the "Curved" plane preset on a 3D solid).

Layer.GeometryPlaneSubdivision.summary: GeometryPlaneSubdivision returns the Plane Subdivision property (1D int, default 4; mesh quality for the curved plane).

Layer.HasAlternateSourceSlot.summary: The slot exists when AE persisted an "ADBE Layer Overrides" +

Layer.HasAudio.summary: HasAudio reports whether the layer's source could carry audio. True when the source resolves to a Footage that is not a solid/placeholder or a Composition (which itself may contain audio layers). For camera / light / null / text / shape layers it returns false.

Layer.HasTrackMatte.summary: HasTrackMatte reports whether this layer uses ANOTHER layer as its alpha/luma matte source. True when TrackMatte != TrackMatteNone.

Layer.HasVideo.summary: HasVideo reports whether the layer has a visual component. True for every non-audio layer kind we model — only pure audio-source layers (AV source with no video stream) would be false, and we don't model that distinction yet. Camera / Light layers have no video output but AE script's `layer.hasVideo` reports false for them, so we mirror that.

Layer.Height.summary: Height returns the layer's effective height in pixels — see Width.

Layer.ID.summary: own layer ID (ldta @0x00) — referenced by ParentID of children

Layer.InPoint.summary: InPoint returns the layer's in-point in seconds (ldta @0x14/@0x18, dividend/divisor pair). Returns 0 if the underlying ldta chunk is absent or too short.

Layer.Index.summary: 0-based timeline position (top of stack = 0; the on-disk Layr order). AE's ExtendScript layer.index is 1-based, so AE-index = Index+1.

Layer.IrisAspectRatio.summary: IrisAspectRatio returns the camera's Iris Aspect Ratio property (1D).

Layer.IrisDiffractionFringe.summary: IrisDiffractionFringe returns the camera's Iris Diffraction Fringe property (1D, %).

Layer.IrisHighlightGain.summary: IrisHighlightGain returns the camera's Iris Highlight Gain property (1D).

Layer.IrisHighlightSaturation.summary: IrisHighlightSaturation returns the camera's Iris Highlight Saturation property (1D).

Layer.IrisHighlightThreshold.summary: IrisHighlightThreshold returns the camera's Iris Highlight Threshold property (1D, 0..1 normalized luminance).

Layer.IrisRotation.summary: IrisRotation returns the camera's Iris Rotation property (1D, degrees).

Layer.IrisRoundness.summary: IrisRoundness returns the camera's Iris Roundness property (1D, %).

Layer.IrisShape.summary: IrisShape returns the camera's Iris Shape menu property (1D, enum: 1=Fast Rectangle, 3..10 = Triangle..Decagon). Nil for non-camera layers.

Layer.Is3D.summary: Flag bits from ldta @0x25-0x27. See parse_layer.go's decoder for exact bit positions.

Layer.IsNameFromSource.summary: IsNameFromSource reports whether the layer's display name is inherited from its source AV item (i.e., the user did not set a custom layer name). True when Name == "" and a source exists.

Layer.IsShapeLayer.summary: IsShapeLayer is true when the layer has an "ADBE Root Vectors Group" property tree (= it's a Shape Layer with vector primitives).

Layer.IsThreeDModelLayer.summary: IsThreeDModelLayer reports whether the layer is a 3D Model layer (AE 24+). Identified by ldta byte 0x83 == 0x05 at parse time; see [inferLayerType].

Layer.IsTrackMatte.summary: IsTrackMatte reports whether this layer is USED AS a matte by any other layer in the same composition. Walks the comp's layers to find references; O(n) on the comp's layer count.

Layer.LayerStylesGroup.summary: LayerStylesGroup returns the layer's "ADBE Layer Styles" subgroup, or nil if absent. Carries Drop Shadow / Bevel / Glow / etc. effect-style sub-properties (separate from the "ADBE Effect Parade" effect list).

Layer.LdtaRawBytes.summary: LdtaRawBytes returns a detached copy of the layer's ldta chunk data, or nil if the layer has no ldta. It is intended for debugging and RE tools.

Layer.LightCastsShadows.summary: LightCastsShadows returns the Casts Shadows toggle if present in the property tree. NOTE: AE may store this as a checkbox flag at the layer level rather than a property, so this accessor returns nil for many real-world projects. The exact ldta location is not RE'd yet.

Layer.LightColor.summary: LightColor returns the light's Color property (4D color or 3D RGB depending on AE version — read Components to disambiguate). Nil for non-light layers.

Layer.LightConeAngle.summary: LightConeAngle returns the spotlight cone-angle property (1D, degrees). Only meaningful for spot lights. Nil otherwise.

Layer.LightConeFeather.summary: LightConeFeather returns the spotlight cone-feather property (1D, %). Only meaningful for spot lights.

Layer.LightFalloffDistance.summary: LightFalloffDistance returns the falloff distance property (1D, pixels).

Layer.LightFalloffStart.summary: LightFalloffStart returns the falloff-start distance property (1D, pixels). Only meaningful when LightFalloffType != None.

Layer.LightFalloffType.summary: LightFalloffType returns the falloff-type menu property (1D enum).

Layer.LightIntensity.summary: LightIntensity returns the light's Intensity property (1D, %). Nil for non-light layers.

Layer.LightKind.summary: light type (Parallel / Spot / Point / Ambient) stored at ldta @0x88; only meaningful when Type == LayerTypeLight

Layer.LightOptionsGroup.summary: LightOptionsGroup returns the light layer's "ADBE Light Options Group", or nil for non-light layers.

Layer.LightShadowDarkness.summary: LightShadowDarkness returns the Shadow Darkness property (1D, %).

Layer.LightShadowDiffusion.summary: LightShadowDiffusion returns the Shadow Diffusion property (1D, pixels).

Layer.LightSource.summary: LightSource returns the layer used as the environment-light source for this Light layer (AE 24+). Returns nil for non-light layers, lights with no source (sentinels 0 / 0xFFFFFFFF), or when the source ID doesn't resolve to a layer in the owning composition.

Layer.LightType.summary: LightType returns the light's Type menu property if present in the property tree. NOTE: AE typically stores the light type at the layer level (similar to LayerType for camera vs light disambig) rather than as a regular property, so this accessor often returns nil for real-world projects — the type field's exact ldta location is not RE'd yet. Kept for future use / older AE versions that may have surfaced it as a property.

Layer.MaskParade.summary: MaskParade returns the layer's "ADBE Mask Parade" subgroup, or nil if absent. For decoded mask data prefer Layer.Masks.

Layer.MaterialCastsShadows.summary: MaterialCastsShadows returns the (shared with Light) Casts Shadows property. On 3D AV layers it carries a tri-state (Off/On/Only); on light layers it's bool. Same property as LightCastsShadows().

Layer.MaterialOptionsGroup.summary: MaterialOptionsGroup returns the 3D AV layer's "ADBE Material Options Group", or nil for 2D layers (Is3D == false).

Layer.Opacity.summary: Opacity returns the layer's Opacity property (1D, 0..1), or nil.

Layer.Orientation.summary: Orientation returns the layer's 3D Orientation property (3 components, degrees per axis — separate from the animatable per-axis RotateX/Y/Z). Present only when Layer.Is3D.

Layer.OutPoint.summary: OutPoint returns the layer's out-point in seconds (ldta @0x1C/@0x20). Returns 0 if the underlying ldta chunk is absent or too short.

Layer.Parent.summary: Parent returns the layer's parent layer, or nil if this layer has no parent (ParentID == 0), the parent ID does not match any layer in the owning composition, or the layer was built outside the parser (no owning comp wired up). AE enforces same-comp parenting; cross-comp lookup is not performed. Returns the immediate parent only — call Parent() on the result to walk the chain.

Layer.Position.summary: Position returns the layer's Position property (3D), or nil.

Layer.PropertyByMatchName.summary: PropertyByMatchName returns the first property on the layer whose MatchName equals name, or nil if no such property exists.

Layer.PropertyByPath.summary: PropertyByPath walks the property hierarchy following each match-name in turn. The last name must resolve to a leaf property; intermediate names must resolve to subgroups. Returns nil if the layer has no tree or any step fails.

Layer.PropertyGroupByMatchName.summary: PropertyGroupByMatchName returns the top-level subgroup of the layer's property tree whose match-name equals name. Equivalent to `l.PropertyTree().Group(name)`. Returns nil when the layer has no tree or the named subgroup isn't present.

Layer.PropertyTree.summary: PropertyTree returns the layer's hierarchical PropertyGroup root, or nil for layers built outside the parser. The root has empty MatchName / Name; its Children are the named top-level groups AE writes under the Layr (Transform, Mask Parade, Effect Parade, etc.).

Layer.RemoveTrackMatte.summary: Alias of [Layer.ClearTrackMatteLayer], kept for API parity with other scripting environments' layer.removeTrackMatte(). Clears both the mode (TrackMatte to None) and the explicit source pointer (TrackMatteLayerID to 0) with one length-preserving write to ldta.

Layer.ReplaceSource.signature: func (l *Layer) ReplaceSource(target AVItem, fixExpressions bool) error
Layer.ReplaceSource.summary: Internally calls the id-based source setter with the target

Layer.RotateX.summary: RotateX / RotateY are the per-axis 3D rotation properties (degrees). Present only when Layer.Is3D; nil otherwise.

Layer.Rotation.summary: Rotation returns the layer's Z-axis Rotation property (1D, degrees), or nil. On 3D layers the X- and Y-rotation properties have different match-names (ADBE Rotate X / ADBE Rotate Y) — use PropertyByMatchName for those.

Layer.Scale.summary: Scale returns the layer's Scale property (3D), or nil.

Layer.SetAlternateSource.summary: Overrides this layer's source through the Essential Properties media-replacement slot. Pass nil (or a zero-id item) to clear the override — equivalent to ClearAlternateSource. Requires the layer to already have an Essential Properties slot: AE only persists the underlying chunk after the source-side layer has been promoted to a motion-graphics template inside its wrapper precomp. If the slot is missing, this errors rather than attempting a structural chunk insertion that would break length-preserving round-trip. When the layer's owning project is known, the item's ID is validated against the project's AV items; an unknown ID returns an error and leaves the bytes untouched. AE additionally rejects items that are not media-replacement compatible (for example a still image standing in for video) at script time; this setter does not replicate that check, and the resulting file still parses cleanly in AE regardless.

Layer.SetAutoOrient.summary: Clears the three mutually-exclusive auto-orient bits spread across ldta offsets 0x25/0x26 and sets the one matching the requested mode. Unknown enum values are treated as None (a no-op clearing of all three bits). The AlongPath mode only has a visible effect when the layer's position has a motion path (keyframes).

Layer.SetCollapseTransform.summary: Collapse Transformations applies to nested-comp layers; Continuously Rasterize applies to Illustrator or shape layers. Both share the same underlying switch bit.

Layer.SetComment.summary: Mirrors AE's "Comments" timeline column / Layer Settings dialog. Encoding mirrors what AE writes: LF becomes CRLF plus a single NUL terminator.

Layer.SetFrameBlendPixelMotion.summary: Only takes effect when FrameBlendEnabled is also true.

Layer.SetFrameInPoint.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via the owning composition's FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based in-point setter. The in-point is source-relative; AE's UI displays startTime plus this value.

Layer.SetFrameOutPoint.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via the owning composition's FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based out-point setter. The out-point is source-relative; AE's UI displays startTime plus this value.

Layer.SetFrameStartTime.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via the owning composition's FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based start-time setter.

Layer.SetInPoint.summary: Refreshes Layer.Duration (= out minus in) after the write.

Layer.SetIsGuide.summary: A guide layer renders in the comp viewer but is excluded from rendered output.

Layer.SetIsNull.summary: AE's UI normally creates null layers via its own dedicated command; flipping this bit post-hoc is accepted by AE but produces uncommon results — only set it when you understand the consequences.

Layer.SetLabel.summary: Indices outside the normal 0..16 range are written verbatim; AE shows index 0 for any unknown value but the byte itself is preserved on round-trip.

Layer.SetLightKind.summary: Only meaningful when the layer's Type is Light; AE silently accepts the byte change on non-light layers but it has no visual effect. The field is present on older project layouts too, so this setter works across the full supported AE range.

Layer.SetLightSource.summary: Stored in the same ldta slot used for the AV SourceID; the field is repurposed depending on Layer.Type. Pass nil to clear, which writes the clear sentinel. Validation requires: the layer must be a Light layer; the target, if non-nil, must be in the same composition; the target must not itself be a Light or Camera layer; the target must not be a 3D layer (3D AV layers cannot drive environment lights); and the target must not be the layer itself. On any validation error the bytes are left unmodified.

Layer.SetLocked.summary: When locked, AE refuses edits in the timeline UI; the underlying file is still mutable through this API.

Layer.SetManualKerning.summary: Writes per-character manual kerning values into the btdk dict. The values slice length must equal the current per-character count (len(TextSource.ManualKerning)). For the values to actually render, the matching style run's AutoKernType must be TextAutoKernNoAuto — toggle it independently via SetRunAutoKernType. Mirrors the AE scripting TextDocument.kerning behavior: the first-character value is also written to the sibling /1/1[0]/0/7 slot, the first-char scalar reflected by the scripting API.

Layer.SetName.summary: Returns an error when the parsed layer has no Utf8 name chunk (unusual — most AE-written layers have one even for default names).

Layer.SetOpacity.summary: Callers that think in percent should divide by 100 first.

Layer.SetParagraphAutoHyphenate.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphAutoHyphenate(paraIdx int, on bool) error
Layer.SetParagraphAutoHyphenate.summary: Splices the auto-hyphenate flag into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph. AE's default is true.

Layer.SetParagraphDirection.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphDirection(paraIdx int, d TextParagraphDirection) error
Layer.SetParagraphDirection.summary: Splices a new paragraph-direction value into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph (btdk paragraph /33). Affects how mixed left-to-right and right-to-left text composes.

Layer.SetParagraphEndIndent.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphEndIndent(paraIdx int, v float64) error
Layer.SetParagraphEndIndent.summary: Splices a new endIndent value into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph.

Layer.SetParagraphFirstLineIndent.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphFirstLineIndent(paraIdx int, v float64) error
Layer.SetParagraphFirstLineIndent.summary: Splices a new firstLineIndent value into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph. The AE 2020 scripting API is a no-op for this attribute on point text; it is writeable from AE 24 onward.

Layer.SetParagraphHangingRoman.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphHangingRoman(paraIdx int, on bool) error
Layer.SetParagraphHangingRoman.summary: Splices the hanging-roman flag into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph (btdk paragraph /21). Only meaningful for box-text.

Layer.SetParagraphJustification.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphJustification(paraIdx int, j TextJustification) error
Layer.SetParagraphJustification.summary: Splices a new justification value into the btdk PostScript paragraph body for the given paragraph.

Layer.SetParagraphLeadingType.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphLeadingType(paraIdx int, lt TextLeadingType) error
Layer.SetParagraphLeadingType.summary: Splices a new leading-type value into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph (btdk paragraph /8).

Layer.SetParagraphSpaceAfter.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphSpaceAfter(paraIdx int, v float64) error
Layer.SetParagraphSpaceAfter.summary: Splices a new spaceAfter value into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph.

Layer.SetParagraphSpaceBefore.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphSpaceBefore(paraIdx int, v float64) error
Layer.SetParagraphSpaceBefore.summary: Splices a new spaceBefore value into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph.

Layer.SetParagraphStartIndent.signature: func (l *Layer) SetParagraphStartIndent(paraIdx int, v float64) error
Layer.SetParagraphStartIndent.summary: Splices a new startIndent value into the btdk paragraph body for the given paragraph.

Layer.SetParent.summary: Pass 0 to clear the parent ("no parent", shown as "None" in the timeline). When the layer lives inside a composition, the new parent ID is validated against same-comp layers — an ID that doesn't resolve returns an error and leaves the bytes untouched. Cross-comp parenting isn't allowed. Setting parentID equal to the layer's own ID is rejected since it would create a self-parent cycle.

Layer.SetRotation.summary: Available on both 2D and 3D layers — it's the only rotation

Layer.SetRunApplyStroke.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunApplyStroke(runIdx int, apply bool) error
Layer.SetRunApplyStroke.summary: Splices the apply-stroke flag into the btdk PostScript body for the given run.

Layer.SetRunAutoKernType.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunAutoKernType(runIdx int, kt TextAutoKernType) error
Layer.SetRunAutoKernType.summary: Splices a new auto-kern-type value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run (btdk style-run /11). Setting it to TextAutoKernNoAuto without also assigning a manual kerning value reads as zero spacing in AE — manual kerning lives in the separate per-character sub-tree at btdk /1/1[0]/0/8, written via SetManualKerning.

Layer.SetRunAutoLeading.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunAutoLeading(runIdx int, auto bool) error
Layer.SetRunAutoLeading.summary: Splices the auto-leading flag into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. When true, the Leading value is computed by AE (typically FontSize x 1.2); when false, the explicit Leading value applies.

Layer.SetRunBaselineOption.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunBaselineOption(runIdx int, base TextBaselineOption) error
Layer.SetRunBaselineOption.summary: Splices a new baseline-option value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. Mirrors the subscript / superscript read-only attributes exposed elsewhere.

Layer.SetRunBaselineShift.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunBaselineShift(runIdx int, shift float64) error
Layer.SetRunBaselineShift.summary: Splices a new baseline-shift value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. Positive values shift the run up.

Layer.SetRunCapsOption.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunCapsOption(runIdx int, caps TextCapsOption) error
Layer.SetRunCapsOption.summary: Splices a new caps-option value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. The underlying btdk byte exists in AE 2020 files too, but the AE 2020 scripting API marks allCaps / smallCaps read-only, so the option is only writeable from AE 24 onward.

Layer.SetRunDigitSet.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunDigitSet(runIdx int, d TextDigitSet) error
Layer.SetRunDigitSet.summary: Splices a new digit-set value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run (btdk style-run /70).

Layer.SetRunFauxBold.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunFauxBold(runIdx int, on bool) error
Layer.SetRunFauxBold.summary: Splices the faux-bold flag into the btdk PostScript body for the given run.

Layer.SetRunFauxItalic.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunFauxItalic(runIdx int, on bool) error
Layer.SetRunFauxItalic.summary: Splices the faux-italic flag into the btdk PostScript body for the given run.

Layer.SetRunFillColor.summary: Splices a new fill color into the btdk PostScript body for the given run, encoded as btdk's [A, R, G, B] array.

Layer.SetRunFontIndex.summary: Splices a new font index into the btdk PostScript body for the given run, referencing an entry in the layer's Fonts table (TextSource.Fonts). The underlying value is a plain integer; the caller is responsible for ensuring the index is in range.

Layer.SetRunFontSize.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunFontSize(runIdx int, sizePts float64) error
Layer.SetRunFontSize.summary: Splices a new font-size value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run.

Layer.SetRunHorizontalScale.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunHorizontalScale(runIdx int, scale float64) error
Layer.SetRunHorizontalScale.summary: Splices a new horizontal-scale value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. AE default is 1; the scripted setter range is 0..100 (see TextStyleRun for unit notes).

Layer.SetRunLeading.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunLeading(runIdx int, leading float64) error
Layer.SetRunLeading.summary: Splices a new leading value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. AE auto-leading is gated by the AutoLeading flag — to make this value take effect the caller should also disable auto-leading via SetRunAutoLeading(runIdx, false), otherwise AE overrides it.

Layer.SetRunLineJoinType.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunLineJoinType(runIdx int, j TextLineJoinType) error
Layer.SetRunLineJoinType.summary: Splices a new line-join-type value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run (btdk style-run /62).

Layer.SetRunNoBreak.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunNoBreak(runIdx int, on bool) error
Layer.SetRunNoBreak.summary: Splices the no-break flag into the btdk PostScript body for the given run (btdk style-run /52). When true, AE won't allow line breaks to fall inside the run.

Layer.SetRunStrokeColor.summary: Splices a new stroke color into the btdk PostScript body for the given run.

Layer.SetRunStrokeOverFill.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunStrokeOverFill(runIdx int, over bool) error
Layer.SetRunStrokeOverFill.summary: Splices the stroke-over-fill flag into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. AE's default is true (stroke renders over fill).

Layer.SetRunStrokeWidth.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunStrokeWidth(runIdx int, width float64) error
Layer.SetRunStrokeWidth.summary: Splices a new stroke-width value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run.

Layer.SetRunTracking.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunTracking(runIdx int, tracking float64) error
Layer.SetRunTracking.summary: Splices a new tracking value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run.

Layer.SetRunTsume.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunTsume(runIdx int, tsume float64) error
Layer.SetRunTsume.summary: Splices a new tsume value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. The setter range is 0..100; the DOM range is 0..1.

Layer.SetRunVerticalScale.signature: func (l *Layer) SetRunVerticalScale(runIdx int, scale float64) error
Layer.SetRunVerticalScale.summary: Splices a new vertical-scale value into the btdk PostScript body for the given run. AE default is 1; the scripted setter range is 0..100 (see TextStyleRun for unit notes).

Layer.SetShy.summary: Shy hides the layer from the shy-filter view in the timeline.

Layer.SetSource.summary: For regular AV layers this is the footage or pre-comp ID. When the owning project is known, sourceID is validated to match an existing Composition or Footage item — an ID that doesn't resolve returns an error and leaves the bytes untouched. Pass 0 to clear (rare; usually turns the layer into a Null-like "no source" stub). AE caches some source-derived metadata (Width/Height) on the layer at render time rather than in ldta, so changing the source preserves the rest of ldta verbatim.

Layer.SetStartTime.summary: AE allows negative start times (pre-roll). Mirrors the change into Layer.StartTime.

Layer.SetStretch.summary: 1.0 is normal speed, 2.0 is 2x slow. Unlike the other time fields, the dividend/divisor pair is split across ldta — the dividend lives near the top, the divisor in the trailing section.

Layer.SetText.summary: The new text may be any length and span any number of paragraphs (split on line breaks): the PostScript string is spliced, the paragraph array is rebuilt with one count-patched entry per paragraph, the style-run array is collapsed to a single run carrying the total count (keeping the first run's style, matching how AE handles a whole-text replace), and the layout cache is left for AE to recompute on load. Empty text is supported and becomes a single empty paragraph. Replacements that keep both the encoded byte length and the per-paragraph UTF-16 counts unchanged are written in place and preserve all runs. A per-character manual-kerning table is dropped on a length-changing replacement, again matching AE's own behavior; the only error case for a well-formed text layer is when the layer isn't actually a text layer. Encoding parity with AE: input is split on line-feed characters (each segment becomes a paragraph terminated by AE's carriage-return convention), then encoded as big-endian UTF-16 with a leading byte-order mark, with PostScript special characters escaped at the byte level. After a successful call Layer.TextSource is re-decoded so subsequent reads reflect the new value.

Layer.SetTimeRemapEnabled.summary: Enabling sets a static value of 0.0 (identity mapping). For

Layer.SetTrackMatte.summary: AE additionally requires the matte source layer to sit immediately above this layer in the comp; this setter only changes the mode byte and does not reorder layers.

Layer.SetTrackMatteLayer.signature: func (l *Layer) SetTrackMatteLayer(sourceID uint32, mode TrackMatteType) error
Layer.SetTrackMatteLayer.summary: Pass sourceID=0 with mode=TrackMatteNone to clear the matte. When the layer lives inside a parsed composition, sourceID is validated against same-comp layers — an ID that doesn't resolve returns an error and leaves the bytes untouched; the matte source must live in the same comp. Setting sourceID equal to the layer's own ID is rejected since self-matte is a no-op in AE and usually indicates a mistake. Passing mode=TrackMatteNone together with a non-zero sourceID means "preserve the target but apply no matte yet" — the source pointer stays while the matte channel stays disabled. On older project files whose ldta layout is shorter, this call errors because the explicit track-matte slot doesn't exist; re-saving the file through a newer AE version first extends ldta so the setter can succeed.

Layer.ShapeContentsGroup.summary: ShapeContentsGroup returns a shape layer's "ADBE Root Vectors Group", or nil for non-shape layers. For typed access prefer the ShapeLayer wrapper (see WrapShapeLayer).

Layer.SourceComposition.summary: SourceComposition returns the composition this layer references as its source (a pre-comp layer), or nil when the source is footage / a solid / any non-composition item, when the SourceID does not resolve to any project item, or when the layer was built outside the parser (no owning comp/project wired up). Use Project.CompositionByID directly for arbitrary lookups.

Layer.SourceFootage.summary: SourceFootage returns the footage item this layer references as its source (a solid / file / placeholder footage), or nil when the source is a composition / no source / outside the parser. Use Project.FootageByName or iterate Project.Footage for arbitrary lookups.

Layer.SourceID.summary: item ID of the layer's source (footage or pre-comp), per ldta@0x28

Layer.StartTime.summary: in-point in seconds (timeline start of the layer)

Layer.TextPropertiesGroup.summary: TextPropertiesGroup returns the layer's "ADBE Text Properties" subgroup, or nil for non-text layers.

Layer.TextSource.summary: TextSource holds the decoded view of TextSourceRaw — text content, fonts, per-run styling, justification. Nil for non-text layers or when the btdk PostScript dict failed to parse (in which case the failure is collected on Project.Warnings).

Layer.TextSourceRaw.summary: TextSourceRaw holds the opaque btds payload for text layers (CoolType PostScript-style serialization of font, size, color, and the actual text string). Nil for non-text layers; kept verbatim for round-trip writeback and downstream tools that need fields beyond TextSource.

Layer.TimeRemap.summary: TimeRemap returns the layer's Time Remap property (1D, seconds) when time remapping is enabled. Returns the property slot even when time remap is disabled — check TimeRemapEnabled() for the on/off bit. To toggle time remap on / off requires structural property-tree changes (AE adds 2 default keyframes); not currently supported.

Layer.TimeRemapEnabled.summary: TimeRemapEnabled reports whether the layer has time remapping turned on. AE always writes the TimeRemap property slot in the property tree (so PropertyByMatchName always finds it on AV layers / precomps), but only populates it with keyframes when remap is enabled — AE adds two default identity keyframes (t=0, t=duration) on enable. When disabled, Keyframes is empty.

Layer.TrackMatteLayer.summary: TrackMatteLayer returns the layer used as this layer's track matte source (AE 23+ explicit pointer at ldta @0xA0). Returns nil when:

Layer.TrackMatteLayerID.summary: explicit matte SOURCE layer ID (ldta @0xA0, AE 23+); 0 = no explicit matte. See Layer.TrackMatteLayer() to resolve to *Layer; SetTrackMatteLayer to assign.

Layer.TransformGroup.summary: TransformGroup returns the layer's "ADBE Transform Group" subgroup, or nil if absent. Standard layers always have it; effect-only layers do not.

Layer.Type.summary: layer kind (AV / shape / text / camera / light / null / adjustment)

Layer.Width.summary: Width returns the layer's effective width in pixels — proxies to the source AV item when present, or to the owning composition's width for layers without an AV source (cameras, lights, nulls, text, shapes). Returns 0 when neither resolves.

LayerQuality.summary: LayerQuality is the layer's render quality (ldta @0x04, uint16).

LayerType.summary: LayerType classifies the kind of layer.

LightKind.summary: LightKind is the layer-level light type stored in ldta @0x88 (4-byte BE uint32, AE 23+ ldta layout). For light layers only; zero for non-light layers (the parser leaves Layer.LightKind as default 0 == Parallel for them, so always cross-check Layer.Type == LayerTypeLight before reading LightKind).

LightKind.String.summary: String returns a human-readable name for the light kind.

Marker.summary: Marker represents a single timeline marker on a layer (or a comp). Times are in seconds. The remaining string fields hold the user- editable annotation data (most are empty unless the user filled them in inside AE's "Marker Dialog").

Marker.Comment.summary: first Utf8 in the Nmrd block

Marker.Duration.summary: seconds; 0 = point marker. Decoded from NmHd @0x08 / 600.

Marker.FrameDuration.summary: FrameDuration returns the marker's duration as an integer frame count. 0 for point markers (Duration == 0).

Marker.FrameTime.summary: FrameTime returns the marker's time as an integer frame count.

Marker.Label.summary: timeline label color index (0..16); 0 = default. NmHd @0x10.

Marker.SetChapter.summary: Rewrites the second Utf8 child of the Nmrd block.

Marker.SetComment.summary: Rewrites the first Utf8 child of the Nmrd block. Use SetChapter / SetURL / SetFrameTarget / SetCuePointName for the other four Utf8 slots — they fill in declaration order, so writing a later slot creates any missing earlier slots as empty.

Marker.SetCuePointName.summary: Rewrites the fifth Utf8 child of the Nmrd block — a legacy Flash-era field, rarely populated in modern AE projects.

Marker.SetDuration.summary: Encoded as a uint32 BE count of 600ths-of-a-second at NmHd offset 0x08. A duration of 0 produces a point marker; negative values clamp to 0.

Marker.SetFrameDuration.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via the owning composition's FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based duration setter.

Marker.SetFrameTarget.summary: Rewrites the fourth Utf8 child of the Nmrd block.

Marker.SetFrameTime.summary: Converts frame back to seconds via the owning composition's FrameRate, then delegates to the seconds-based time setter.

Marker.SetLabel.summary: Indices outside the 0..16 label range are written verbatim — AE displays index 0 for unrecognized values but the byte still round-trips.

Marker.SetURL.summary: Rewrites the third Utf8 child of the Nmrd block.

Marker.Time.summary: marker position in seconds, decoded via the owning composition's TickRate

Mask.Closed.summary: from shph[3] bit3 clear (0x01 closed / 0x09 open)

Mask.Color.summary: R, G, B from mkif @0x2D-0x2F (timeline label color)

Mask.Feather.summary: Other mask-level properties, populated when their cdat values exist in the mask atom's property tree. Feather is 2D (X, Y) in pixels; Opacity is 0..1; Expansion (AE's "Mask Expansion", internally "ADBE Mask Offset") is in pixels.

Mask.Index.summary: from mkif @0x08 (AE internal mask ID, not always sequential)

Mask.Locked.summary: from mkif @0x01 (== 1 when AE timeline UI lock is on)

Mask.MkifRaw.summary: 48 bytes raw mask info (preserved for write-back)

Mask.Name.summary: from omtn, falling back to the atom tdgp's tdsn (where AE persists the panel name)

Mask.PathKeyframes.summary: nil when path is not animated

Mask.Properties.summary: Properties is every other tdmn+tdbs leaf inside the mask atom's property group (anything beyond Shape/Feather/Opacity/Offset, or those when keyframed). Useful for keyframed mask properties (e.g. animated feather).

Mask.SetClosed.summary: For animated masks this only affects the first snapshot; per-keyframe closed flags aren't exposed yet.

Mask.SetColor.summary: AE always keeps the alpha byte at 0xFF; this setter does not touch it.

Mask.SetExpansion.summary: Internally this is the `ADBE Mask Offset` property (AE's UI calls it "Mask Expansion"). Positive values grow the masked region, negative values shrink it. The leaf is elided by AE when at its default, so setting it materializes the leaf in the mask's atom group.

Mask.SetFeather.summary: The `ADBE Mask Feather` leaf is elided by AE when at its default, so setting it materializes the leaf in the mask's atom group.

Mask.SetLocked.summary: When locked, AE refuses edits to the mask in the timeline UI; the underlying bytes are still mutable through this library.

Mask.SetOpacity.summary: Mask Opacity scales how strongly the mask reveals or cuts — at 0.5 a reveal shows the layer at half strength. The `ADBE Mask Opacity` leaf is elided by AE when at its default, so setting it materializes the leaf in the mask's atom group.

Mask.Vertices.summary: first snapshot (or only one when static)

MaskMode.summary: MaskMode is the compositing mode for a mask (matches AE C++ SDK values).

It mirrors SetMaskPath's BezierPath input rather than the MaskVertex-based MaskPathKeyframe parse output, so callers build paths the same way for static and animated masks.

MaskPathKeyframe.summary: MaskPathKeyframe is one keyframe of an animated mask path. Time is in seconds. Vertices is the full path snapshot at that time. Easing follows the same scalar (one TemporalEase per side) layout as spatial keyframes.

Project.summary: Project holds the fully parsed contents of an .aep file.

Project.AVItemByID.summary: AVItemByID returns the *Composition or *Footage with the given id, or nil if no AV item in the project matches (or id == 0). Folders are not AV items and are not consulted.

Project.AudioSampleRate.summary: AudioSampleRate returns the project's audio sample rate in Hz. Returns 0 when the adfr chunk is absent or too short.

Project.ColorManagementSystem.summary: ColorManagementSystem returns the color management system used by the project. Returns ColorManagementSystemAdobe (0) when CMS chunk is absent.

Project.CompensateForSceneReferredProfil.summary: CompensateForSceneReferredProfiles reports whether AE compensates for scene-referred profiles when rendering (acer byte 0 != 0). Returns false when the chunk is absent.

Project.CompositionByID.summary: CompositionByID returns the first composition whose ID matches id, or nil if no such composition exists. ID 0 is treated as no-match (mirrors Composition.LayerByID; real AE projects start item IDs at 1). Footage and Folder items share the same ID namespace but are stored in separate slices, so an ID belonging to a non-composition item returns nil here.

Project.CompositionByName.summary: CompositionByName returns the first composition whose Name matches the given string, or nil if none does. Matching is exact (case-sensitive). Comp names aren't guaranteed unique in AE; use CompositionByID when you need precise identity.

Project.DisplayStartFrame.summary: DisplayStartFrame returns the display start frame (0 or 1). This is derived from frames_count_type % 2. Returns 0 when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.EffectNames.summary: EffectNames returns the match-names of every effect referenced by the project, from the root-level `Pefl` LIST → `pjef` Utf8 entries. Returns nil when the project has no Pefl LIST (e.g., projects with no effects applied anywhere or builder-synthesized projects).

Project.ExpressionEngine.summary: ExpressionEngine returns the project's expression engine name ("extendscript" or "javascript-1.0"). Defaults to "extendscript" when the ExEn chunk is absent.

Project.FeetFramesFilmType.summary: FeetFramesFilmType returns the film type for feet+frames timecode display. Returns FeetFramesFilmTypeMM35 (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.FootageByName.summary: FootageByName returns the first footage item whose Name matches the given string, or nil if none does. Matching is exact (case-sensitive).

Project.FootageTimecodeDisplayStartType.summary: FootageTimecodeDisplayStartType returns how timecode is displayed for footage. Returns FootageTimecodeDisplayStartTypeStart0 (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.Footages.summary: Footages returns the project's footage items (alias of the Project.Footage slice field, provided as a convenience).

Project.FramesCountType.summary: FramesCountType returns how frames are counted in the project. Returns FramesCountTypeStart0 (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.FramesUseFeetFrames.summary: FramesUseFeetFrames returns whether frames use feet+frames display. Returns false when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.GpuAccelType.summary: GpuAccelType returns the project's GPU acceleration device id (UUID-style string inside the gpuG LIST → Utf8 child). We surface the raw string since AE writes a runtime-resolved device UUID. Empty string when the chunk is absent.

Project.LayerByID.summary: LayerByID searches every composition in the project for a layer with the matching ID and returns the first hit. Returns nil for id == 0 (the "no layer" sentinel) and when no comp owns this id.

Project.LinearBlending.summary: LinearBlending reports whether the project uses linear blending (presence of lnrb chunk under root).

Project.LinearizeWorkingSpace.summary: LinearizeWorkingSpace reports whether the working color space is linearized for blending (presence of lnrp chunk under root).

Project.LutInterpolationMethod.summary: LutInterpolationMethod returns the LUT interpolation method. Returns LutInterpolationMethodTrilinear (0) when CMS chunk is absent.

Project.MarshalJSON.summary: MarshalJSON serializes the Project as JSON.

Project.OcioConfigurationFile.summary: OcioConfigurationFile returns the OCIO configuration file path. Returns empty string when CMS chunk is absent.

Project.ParseWarnings.summary: ParseWarnings is the structured companion to Warnings. New code should use this when it needs machine-readable warning context; Warnings remains the stable human-readable view and transaction signal.

Project.RenderQueue.summary: RenderQueue holds the parsed render queue (LIST:LRdr). Nil when the project has no LRdr chunk; non-nil with empty Items for an empty queue. Read-only (P3 §3A slice-1).

Project.Revision.summary: Revision returns the project's file Revision counter — incremented by AE on each save. Read-only here since the head chunk also carries the next-item-id counter that our writer manages independently. Returns 0 when the file has no head chunk or its data is too short.

Project.RootFolder.summary: RootFolder returns the project's root folder. AE projects always have a root folder at the top of the items tree; we return the first Folder slice entry, or nil when the project was built without folders (synthesized minimal fixtures).

Project.SetBitsPerChannel.summary: Writes to BOTH the nhed offset 0x0F and nnhd offset 0x18 header bytes — AE stores the enum redundantly, so both copies are kept in sync. Accepts the BPC8 / BPC16 / BPC32 constants; other values are written verbatim (in case AE introduces e.g. half-float later) but produce a less obvious AE UI state.

Project.SetDisplayStartFrame.summary: Implemented by modifying frames_count_type, which shares the same nnhd byte 20 written by SetFramesCountType, so the two setters are transitively gated together.

Project.SetExpressionEngine.summary: Refuses when the project has no ExEn chunk yet, rather than synthesizing one — adding a new top-level LIST requires its own AE ship-gate verification.

Project.TimeDisplayType.summary: TimeDisplayType returns how time is displayed in the project. Returns TimeDisplayTypeTimecode (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.TimecodeDefaultBase.summary: TimecodeDefaultBase returns the default timecode base (1-999). Returns 0 when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.ToJSON.summary: ToJSON converts the Project to a JSON-serializable view.

Project.TransparencyGridThumbnails.summary: TransparencyGridThumbnails returns whether transparency grid is shown in thumbnails. Returns false when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.Warnings.summary: Warnings collects non-fatal parsing anomalies — chunks whose header looked sane enough to attempt decoding but whose payload did not match the expected layout (length mismatch, impossible counts, etc). Each entry is a human-readable string kept for compatibility and mutation rollback checks; ParseWarnings carries the structured form. Empty (nil) on a clean parse.

Project.WorkingGamma.summary: WorkingGamma returns the working gamma value (2.2 or 2.4) per the dwga byte 0 selector (0 → 2.2, non-zero → 2.4). Returns 2.2 default when dwga is absent.

Project.WorkingSpace.summary: WorkingSpace returns the working color space name (R only). Returns "None" when the chunk is absent or has no baseColorProfile.

Project.WriteAEP.summary: Sizes are recomputed from the current chunk data, so mutations such as Footage.SetPath that change byte lengths are handled correctly. This is best-effort write-back: only a small subset of the .aep format is understood, and chunks that aren't recognized pass through byte-for-byte. The scene-graph to chunk sync (shape layers / render queue / guides / head counters) runs in the writer back-ref before the RIFX tree is written, so this method itself never touches chunk bytes directly.

Project.XmpPacket.summary: XmpPacket returns the project's XMP metadata packet (trailing UTF-8 XML after the RIFX root chunk). Returns "" when the file has no XMP trailer or the project was built outside the parser.

Property.summary: Property represents an animatable layer property.

Property.Active.summary: Active is an alias for Enabled, provided as a convenience. Kept as a separate accessor even though it's a thin wrapper.

Property.CanVaryOverTime.summary: CanVaryOverTime reports whether AE will accept keyframes on this property. Most properties can; group containers and some metadata-only properties cannot. Read from tdb4 @0x0B bit 1.

Property.Components.summary: 1 for scalar, 2 for 2D point, 3 for 3D point, etc.

Property.ControlType.summary: ControlType returns the UI control type for the property (scalar slider, color picker, angle dial, etc.). Derived from tdb4 flags.

Property.DefaultValue.summary: DefaultValue is the property's default value (what AE considers the "unmodified" state). For transform properties, set from hardcoded tables during parse; for effect parameters, from pard chunks. nil when unknown (non-transform, non-effect properties).

Property.DimensionsSeparated.summary: DimensionsSeparated reports whether a multidimensional property has its dimensions split into separate per-axis followers (AE's "Separate Dimensions" on Position). Read from tdsb byte 3 (_enable_flags) bit 1; defaults to false when the tdsb chunk is absent. Only the leader (the "ADBE Position" property) carries this flag set. W (the structural separate/merge toggle) is deferred — it restructures the property group.

Property.Elided.summary: Elided reports whether the property is hidden from the AE UI. This is set for parser-synthesized placeholder groups; we don't synthesize anything yet, so this always returns false. Reserved for future implementations that materialize missing slots.

Property.Enabled.summary: Enabled reports whether the property is enabled (UI toggle next to the property name in AE's timeline). Read from tdsb byte 3 bit 0; defaults to true when the tdsb chunk is absent.

Property.Expression.summary: JS expression source, "" when no expression set

Property.ExpressionEnabled.summary: tdb4 @0x77 disabled byte (0 = AE evaluates; @0x78 is the has-expression marker). Always true for properties without an expression (AE's default state)

Property.Gradient.summary: Gradient holds the parsed gradient data for "ADBE Vector Grad Colors" properties. The XML is stored in the cdat chunk and parsed during property initialization. nil for non-gradient properties.

Property.IsAnimated.summary: IsAnimated reports whether the property has keyframes. When the tdb4 chunk is available it reads the explicit animated flag (byte 0x44 bool); otherwise it falls back to len(Keyframes) > 0.

Property.IsColor.summary: IsColor reports whether the property is a color (RGBA). 4-channel color properties like Fill Color, Tritone Highlights/Midtones/Shadows. Read from tdb4 @0x3B bit 0.

Property.IsInteger.summary: IsInteger reports whether the property is integer-valued (some dropdowns / enum knobs). Read from tdb4 @0x3B bit 2.

Property.IsModified.summary: IsModified reports whether the property has been changed from its default state. A property is considered modified when it has keyframes, has an expression (regardless of enabled state), or its StaticValue differs from DefaultValue. Does not yet cover the always-modified special-cases (Source Text, mask-index, effect-NoValue) which depend on parser context we don't yet track.

Property.IsNameSet.summary: IsNameSet reports whether the property has an explicit display name set (different from its match-name). Currently a thin proxy: `Name != "" && Name != MatchName`. The display name lives in the underlying tdsn Utf8 chunk; our parser doesn't yet decode tdsn into Property.Name (always defaults to MatchName), so this returns false for parsed properties until tdsn decode lands.

Property.IsNoValue.summary: IsNoValue reports whether the property has no stored value (group-like properties, dropdown markers). Read from tdb4 @0x39 bit 0.

Property.IsSeparationFollower.summary: IsSeparationFollower reports whether the property is a per-axis component of a separated multidimensional property (X / Y / Z Position).

Property.IsSeparationLeader.summary: IsSeparationLeader reports whether the property is the multidimensional leader that can be separated into per-axis followers — true for "ADBE Position" regardless of whether it is currently separated (use DimensionsSeparated for the actual state).

Property.IsSpatial.summary: IsSpatial reports whether the property is spatial (motion-path) — Position and Anchor Point are spatial; Scale / Rotate / Opacity are not. Read from tdb4 @0x05 bit 3.

Property.IsVector.summary: IsVector reports whether the property is a vector type — multi-axis point properties like Position, Scale. Read from tdb4 @0x3B bit 3.

Property.LastValue.summary: LastValue is the property's last-set value from the pard chunk (effect parameters only). nil for non-effect properties.

Property.LayerRefID.summary: tdpi-bound layer reference for layer-picker effect params

Property.LockedRatio.summary: LockedRatio reports whether the property's locked ratio flag is set. Read from tdsb @0x02 bit 4 (byte 2 bit 4).

Property.MaxValue.summary: MaxValue returns the maximum permitted value for the property, or nil if no tduM chunk is present.

Property.MinValue.summary: MinValue returns the minimum permitted value for the property, or nil if no tdum chunk is present. Type depends on property kind: float64 for scalars, []float64 for multi-component, float64 (from uint32) for integer properties.

Property.NbOptions.summary: NbOptions is the number of options for enum/dropdown effect parameters (pard chunk). 0 for non-enum properties.

Property.OwnerLayer.summary: OwnerLayer walks from a parsed leaf up to the synthetic property-tree root and returns the owning Layer, or nil when the property was built outside the parser / lives under an Effect or Mask subtree (those roots carry no layer back-ref). Exported for the serializer stage (internal/aep).

Property.ParentGroup.summary: ParentGroup returns the AEPropertyGroup that contains this property in the layer's hierarchical property tree, or nil when the property was built outside the parser, lives inside an Effect/Mask (not the layer-level tdgp), or hasn't been wired through wirePropertyTreeLeaves.

Property.PropertyDepth.summary: PropertyDepth returns the number of levels of parent groups between this property and the containing layer. Returns 0 for top-level property groups (Transform, Effects, etc.), 1 for their direct children, and so on. Returns -1 when the property has no parent tree group wired up.

Property.PropertyIndex.summary: PropertyIndex returns the 0-based position of this property within its parent AEPropertyGroup, or -1 when the property has no parent group (i.e. was built outside the parser or is a top-level item).

Property.PropertyMatchName.summary: PropertyMatchName returns the property's AE match-name (e.g. "ADBE Position"). Implements PropertyBase.

Property.PropertyName.summary: PropertyName returns the property's display name. Implements PropertyBase.

Property.SeparationDimension.summary: SeparationDimension returns the axis a separation follower represents (0 = X, 1 = Y, 2 = Z), or -1 when the property is not a follower. (-1 means the property is not a follower.)

Property.UnitsText.summary: UnitsText returns the text description of the units for the property (e.g. "pixels", "degrees", "percent", "seconds", "dB"). Returns "" when the property has no known unit.

Property.ValuePropertyType.summary: PropertyValueType returns the type of value stored in the property (OneD, TwoD, ThreeD, Color, NoValue, etc.). Derived from tdb4 flags.
